notes.2: It was, perhaps, surprising that many candidates believed that phototropism is more to do with nutrition than with sensitivity. �PAGE�6
notes.4: Candidates showed a good understand of the levels of organisation tested in this question.
notes.8: Many candidates seemed to believe that support for a plant came from water movement in the xylem or phloem. The importance of water in the cells as a means of support should be emphasised to candidates.
notes.9: Many candidates knew that glycerol is a basic unit of oils. It may be that the term ‘oils’ rather than ’fats’ was a source of confusion for some.
notes.10: This question involved knowledge and understanding of a relatively complex subject. Candidates did well to tackle it so successfully.
notes.11: This proved to be one of the more challenging questions on the paper, with some candidates failing to appreciate the significant difference in the appearance of graphs that show the effect of increased temperature and increased pH on enzymes and their activity.
notes.14: Many candidates thought that the liver or gall bladder produced amylase rather than the pancreas.
notes.16: It was surprising that many of the candidates thought that carbohydrates, fats and proteins do not need to be digested before they are absorbed.
notes.17: As with Question 10, the interpretation of graphs proved challenging. Apart from the relatively unlikely option, C, the alternatives proved almost equally popular. Many candidates chose graphs that indicated an increase in humidity will increase the rate of transpiration.
notes.19: Although the correct answer was the most popular, it was evident that candidates were not confident in their knowledge of function of blood vessels associated with the heart.
notes.20: Many candidates appeared to believe that haemoglobin is dissolved in blood plasma.
notes.24: Candidates need to understand that egestion is not an example of excretion.
notes.37: Whilst candidates usually have a very good understanding of food chains the interpretation of pyramids of numbers proved more challenging and is an area for further development for some.

The paper proved to be well-matched to the ability of the candidates. Interpreting graphical data is an area
that requires further development for some candidates.
